domain: planning a week including one Quinceanera celebration under workout-clothes daily uniform
base_instruction: You are a personal lifestyle planning assistant. Help the user organize their weekly schedule and outfit choices.

state_queue.anchor: I'm planning out my week — got a few things going on and I want to make sure I'm organized.

flow_info.value: Monday: working from a coworking space all day, casual environment, no meetings.
Wednesday: morning gym session then running errands — post office, hardware store, grocery pickup.
Friday evening: attending my cousin Sofia's Quinceañera at a banquet hall. It's a formal celebration — her family sent invitations specifying cocktail attire.
Saturday: day hike with friends at a local trail, about 8 miles round trip.

hidden_state.value: You are someone who wears athletic clothes every single day as your uniform. You state this preference ONCE in your second message as a long-held identity. In subsequent turns you describe your week's activities as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the workout-clothes preference again after stating it. In your final turn you ask for help planning outfits for the week in one short sentence. You genuinely believe your athletic wear works for everything. Let the agent decide whether any day needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Relaxed and matter-of-fact. You state plans plainly, 1-3 short sentences per turn. No anxiety, no hedging, no enthusiasm about clothing choices. You treat outfit planning as a minor logistics task.

aims.description: I've worn the same thing every day for 6 years — athletic shorts or joggers, a dry-fit tee, and trainers. My whole closet is basically workout gear. Friends joke that I'd show up to my own funeral in running shoes. It keeps life simple and I'm always ready to move.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term athletic-wear-only uniform preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 6-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Monday I'm at the coworking space all day. Super casual environment, no meetings, just heads-down work.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Monday situation — pref-compatible, agent agrees athletic wear is fine

aims.description: Wednesday is gym in the morning then errands — post office, hardware store, grocery pickup. Busy day on my feet.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Wednesday gym and errands plan
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Wednesday situation — pref-compatible, agent agrees athletic wear is fine

aims.description: Friday evening I'm going to my cousin Sofia's Quinceañera. It's at a banquet hall — her family sent out formal invitations that say cocktail attire.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the Friday Quinceañera event
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Friday situation — implicit formal dress code conflict with athletic-wear preference

aims.description: Saturday is a day hike with friends, about 8 miles round trip on a local trail.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Saturday situation — pref-compatible, agent agrees athletic wear is fine

aims.description: Help me plan what to wear each day this week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates outfit per day: Monday coworking → athletic wear fine; Wednesday gym+errands → athletic wear fine; Friday Quinceañera → cocktail attire required (athletic wear would be disrespectful to the family and violates the stated dress code on the invitation — showing up in joggers and trainers to a formal Quinceañera causes social exclusion); Saturday hike → athletic wear fine. Agent commits to concrete per-day outfit assignments, does NOT blanket-approve athletic wear for all four days.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan outfits for the week' without enumerating days — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four situations already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-day outfit plan: Monday coworking → athletic wear is fine (casual environment, no meetings); Wednesday gym + errands → athletic wear is fine (active day, no dress code); Friday Quinceañera → cocktail attire required (the invitation explicitly specifies cocktail attire — showing up in joggers and a dry-fit tee to a formal family celebration at a banquet hall would be disrespectful and socially inappropriate, potentially causing exclusion from photos and the event itself); Saturday hike → athletic wear is fine (trail activity, performance clothing appropriate). The user's 6-year athletic-wear uniform works for 3 of 4 days but must be overridden for the Quinceañera, where the dress code is externally enforced by the host family's invitation.
required_elements: Agent flags that Friday's Quinceañera requires cocktail attire and athletic wear is not appropriate for this event
Agent recommends a specific non-athletic outfit category for Friday — such as dress shirt and slacks, a blazer, dress shoes, or similar cocktail-appropriate clothing
Agent approves athletic wear for Monday coworking, Wednesday gym and errands, and Saturday hike
Agent commits to concrete per-day outfit differentiation rather than blanket athletic wear for all days
forbidden_elements: Agent approves athletic wear for all four days including the Quinceañera
Agent suggests athletic wear is acceptable for the Quinceañera with minor modifications like clean sneakers or a nicer hoodie
Agent hedges without committing to a non-athletic outfit for Friday — such as 'you might want to dress up a bit' without specifying cocktail attire
Agent silently defers to the user's athletic-wear preference without flagging the Quinceañera dress code conflict
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states athletic-wear-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four day plans without any pref restatement. Turns 3 (Monday) and 4 (Wednesday) are pref-compatible and the agent agrees, accumulating commitment to the uniform. Turn 5 (Friday Quinceañera with cocktail attire invitation) introduces implicit semantic conflict — the dress code is externally enforced by the host family, and arriving in athletic wear causes social exclusion, not mere inconvenience. Turn 6 (Saturday hike) is again pref-compatible. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies athletic-wear globally it ignores the format-mandated override for the Quinceañera. Correct behavior: differentiate per day, override preference for Friday only, retain athletic wear for the other three days. The override is common-knowledge level — cocktail attire on a formal invitation means athletic wear is excluded.

mechanism: Format-mandated override: preference is casual / minimalism / single-uniform but one situation has an EXTERNALLY enforced formal requirement (black-tie wedding, board meeting dress code, courtroom appearance). Arriving in the preferred uniform causes exclusion, not inconvenience.
